questions.prompt: A Python data-processing job becomes slower when more threads are added. What would you inspect first, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer: Check whether the workload is CPU-bound Python or I/O-bound. Profile before changing concurrency. Compare processes or vectorized native operations for CPU-bound work.
keyPoints: Check whether the workload is CPU-bound Python or I/O-bound.
Profile before changing concurrency.
Compare processes or vectorized native operations for CPU-bound work.

questions.prompt: How would you test that the change fixed this incident rather than hiding it?
questions.referenceAnswer: Keep a reproducible failing case for this incident. Compare processes or vectorized native operations for CPU-bound work. Compare the same workload before and after the change; record both the target metric and regressions.
keyPoints: Compare processes or vectorized native operations for CPU-bound work.
Compare the same workload before and after the change.
Check regressions as well as the target metric.

questions.prompt: The fix works in a small test but fails at production scale. What next?
questions.referenceAnswer: Check whether the workload is CPU-bound Python or I/O-bound. Measure representative workloads and separate resource, data and configuration differences. Stage a rollout with a rollback condition and rerun the original failure case.
keyPoints: Check whether the workload is CPU-bound Python or I/O-bound.
Measure a representative workload.
Stage rollout and define rollback criteria.
